question: What does the Game Dashboard include?
gold_answer: The Game Dashboard shows head-to-head detail for a single game. It includes Player Stats, Team Stats, Roster, and Play-by-Play. You also get an individual player breakdown for both teams (switch categories such as Rushing vs. Receiving with a dropdown), a side-by-side team stats comparison for home and away, and game rosters with a toggle for starters or the full roster. Open it from search results, or from the Dashboard click View Full Schedule and then any game card.

rag.answer: The Game Dashboard shows head-to-head detail for one game. It includes Player Stats (with a Category dropdown for stat types), Team Stats in a side-by-side comparison for both teams, Rosters for both teams (with a Show dropdown for starters vs full roster), and Play-by-Play of every action in the match.

okf.answer: The Game Dashboard shows head-to-head detail for a single game. From a specific matchup you get an individual player breakdown for every player on both teams (switch stat categories such as Rushing vs Receiving with a dropdown), a side-by-side team stats comparison for home and away, and game rosters with a toggle for starters or the full roster. Open it from search results, or from the Dashboard choose View Full Schedule and click a game card.

mixed.answer: The Game Dashboard shows head-to-head detail for one game. It includes Player Stats, Team Stats, roster information, and Play-by-Play. You also get per-player stats for both teams (category dropdown), side-by-side team stats, and rosters with a starters vs full roster toggle. Reach it from search results or via View Full Schedule on the Dashboard, then any game card.

question: What can Visualize Data do?
gold_answer: Visualize Data adds simple charts to search results. After a search, click the Visualize Data button near the results table to show a chart for the query and period (game or season). It is available on Search Result Screens when a query returns at least one row. Supported query types are Simple, Complex, Records, Last Time When, and Streaks. Simple queries use a horizontal bar chart of the top 10 players who met the condition most often, with number of occurrences. Complex queries use a scatter plot of the top 10 players who met both conditions most frequently. Records (min and max) use a line chart of the first 10 result rows, with each player's record game in the center and up to 3 games before and after. Last Time When uses a line chart of unique players from the results, plotting up to 10 of their games.

It is available on Search Result Screens when at least one row is returned. Supported query types include Simple, Complex, Records, Last Time When, and Streaks. Simple queries show a horizontal bar chart of the top 10 players who met the condition most often. Complex queries use a scatter plot for the top 10 who met both conditions most frequently. Record queries use a line chart of the first 10 result rows, centering each player's record game with up to three games before and after. Last Time When plots unique players from the results, up to 10 of their games. Run a search, click Visualize Data on the top right of the table, then close the panel to return to the table.

question: What are Season Highs on the Team Dashboard?
gold_answer: Season Highs on the Team Dashboard shows the highest value the team achieved for each statistic in a season, plus the game date it was recorded. Click SEASON HIGHS in the header. You can filter by Season, Category, and Substat. The table columns are Stat Name, Value, and Game Date. Apply filters with the dropdowns, click x to clear, and click any column header to sort.

question: How do I export report records?
gold_answer: Export saves your search results locally for offline analysis and record-keeping. Run a search on the Athlyte Search Dashboard, then on the results page click Export at the top right of the table. The system generates a file of your current results. A .xlsx file downloads with the same rows shown in the table, including any filters you applied.

rag.answer: Run your search on the Athlyte Search Dashboard. On the results page, click Export at the top right of the table. The system generates a file of your current results as an Excel (.xlsx) download to your default download folder, including the rows visible in the table with any filters applied.

okf.answer: Perform your search on the Athlyte Search Dashboard, then click Export at the top right of the results page. The system automatically generates a file with your current results. Downloads are Excel (.xlsx) files saved to your device's default download folder and include all data visible in the results table.

question: What filters can I apply to search results?
gold_answer: You can refine results in the sidebar without retyping the query. Sidebar filters apply to all query types except Streaks: Opponent and Conference, Game Result (Wins or Losses), Game Type (Regular Season vs Post-season), Date Range, Player Metadata (Name, Position, or Class year), and Period Type (such as first half or overtime). You can also put filters in the search text: team name, conference, or division; player name, class, or position; and game result or game type. On Team results, the Position filter is hidden.

rag.answer: Athlyte Search includes sidebar filters to refine results. They apply to all query types except Streaks. Available filters include Results (match result), Date (custom date range by match date), Name (specific player), and Period Type (time period within a game). For Season queries, the panel also shows Position and Classes.

okf.answer: Use the sidebar to refine results without retyping your query. These filters apply to all query types except Streaks: Opponent and Conference, Game Result (Wins or Losses), Game Type (Regular Season vs Post-season), Date Range, Player Metadata (Name, Position, or Class year), and Period Type (such as first half or overtime). You can also add qualifiers in the search text for team, opponent, conference, division, player name, class, position, game result, and game type. On Team result screens, the Position filter is hidden.

mixed.answer: Refine results from the sidebar; filters apply to all query types except Streaks. Options include match result (Results), custom Date range, player Name, Period Type, plus Opponent and Conference, Game Type, and player metadata (Position, Class) where shown. You can also narrow queries with in-text qualifiers for teams, opponents, conferences, players, and game context. Team results hide the Position filter.

question: What periods are supported for basic queries in Men's Football?
gold_answer: For basic queries in Men's Football (MFB), supported periods are Quarter, Half, Game, Season, and Career. Career is available for Player stats only, not Team stats. A sport must be selected before starting a query.

question: What is Athlyte Query Language (AQL)?
gold_answer: Athlyte Query Language (AQL) is the structured query format Athlyte Search uses after a natural language query is transformed so a program or database can fetch the right information. The standard fields are query_type, entity, qualifiers, stat_period, conditions, streak_len, periods, and period_type. For example, the query "The highest punt returns yards accomplished during a season" becomes query_type max, entity player, stat_period season, and conditions s_punt_returns_yards.

Standard fields include query_type, entity, qualifiers, stat_period, conditions, streak_len, periods, and period_type. Example: "The highest punt returns yards accomplished during a season" maps to query_type max, entity player, stat_period season, and conditions s_punt_returns_yards.
